title.from: API-first standard (ADR-0007): every PF capability exposes a secured API; tooling is a client only
title.to: API-first standard (ADR-0007): assess API need per capability; where needed, expose a secured API for internal + external consumers

to.implementation_strategy: Leverage core/capability_bridge.py and core/capability_packs.py as the registry; formalize each PF capability behind a secured HTTP API (authn/z via existing capability vectors). CLI/tooling becomes a thin client of the API. Codify ADR-0007 as docs/adr/0007-api-first.md plus an enforcement check (lint/CI) verifying every pack entry has an API route registered.
dependency_findings: BI-1265 event bus provides transport patterns REUSE for API security/middleware
BI-0123 capability wiring defines authz model REQUIRES settled
conflict_findings: BI-1265 may touch same transport/auth middleware concurrently
BI-0122 could double-register routes if not coordinated
duplication_findings: BI-0122 'API-first exposure for all new pipeline capabilities' overlaps; scope it as a subset and mark RELATED
capability_bridge already exposes programmatic access; avoid rebuilding a second registry
to.rationale: Enshrines API-first as a codified, enforced standard with minimal new code by extending the existing capability registry/bridge; tooling demoted to client role.
assumptions: capability_bridge is the SSOT for capability discovery
An authn/z mechanism (tokens/RBAC) already exists or is funded
PF runs as a long-lived service able to host HTTP routes
risks: Legacy capabilities lacking API surface force wide refactor scope
Auth enforcement may lag, creating interim insecure endpoints
evidence: core/capability_bridge.py and core/capability_packs.py exist as candidate reuse points
config/capability-packs.json enumerates capabilities
missing_info: Which authn/z stack (OIDC, mTLS, API keys) is mandated
Backlog coverage inventory: which capabilities currently lack APIs
Owner assignment for ADR ratification
